newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GIB says still seeking partner for Inno.
newsitem.headline: GIB says still seeking partner for Inno.

text.p: Belgian retail group GIB said it was still seeking a partner for its department store chain Inno.

"It will take time to find Inno a partner. One day we'll find one, but I can't say when - the big magazine chains (in Europe) are not really expanding," GIB's chief executive officer Diego du Monceau told a news conference.
GIB said Inno finished the financial year to January 31 at breakeven, though it made an operating profit. Despite a sluggish textiles market sales edged up 0.5 percent to 8.4 billion francs.
GIB made a group net profit of 3.39 billion francs in 1996/97 after a group loss of 4.39 billion (due to a 5.53 billion extraordinary loss) the year before.
Asked about the outlook generally for the GIB group in 1997, Du Monceau said it was too early to make a forecast.
"It depends on the economy, the weather, a pickup in consumption at (burger unit) Quick Restaurants," he said, noting "we have no big problem companies at the moment."

GIB plans to invest seven billion Belgian francs in 1997/98, and its priorities for the year include reinforcing the competitiveness of its super- and hypermarkets, redefining its local neighbourhood store concept, and developing supermarket unit GB's commercial agreement with France's Promodes.
It also wanted to continue the expansion of its European do-it-yourself (DIY) operations, to continue the recovery at its U.S. DIY unit Scotty's, and to make Quick more competitive and grow.

European DIY sales rose 0.7 percent in 1996/97 despite poor weather. Scotty's reported an increase of 3.1 percent in dollar sales, which, combined with careful cost control, helped the chain to double operating profit to $12.5 million, GIB said.
